title: China’s AI Diplomacy Is Working
gist: Teaser (paywalled after the intro) by Daniel Remler: China's AI diplomacy is working and the US should take notes; the hope that AI-safety cooperation with Beijing can be siloed off from strategic competition is 'as appealing as it is fanciful'.

themes.theme: US-China AI talks inside strategic competition

insights.claim: The Biden administration paired sweeping technology restrictions on China with only a narrow bilateral dialogue on AI risk.
insights.speaker: Daniel Remler
insights.so_what: Baseline: US policy toolkit has been export controls first, dialogue second.
insights.quote: The Biden administration paired sweeping technology restrictions with a narrow dialogue on risk
insights.locator: Can the United States and China

insights.claim: The Trump administration has kept a US-China AI channel open while downplaying AI safety.
insights.speaker: Daniel Remler
insights.so_what: Open channel with low safety emphasis suggests talks are transactional/competitive rather than risk-focused.
insights.quote: the Trump administration has kept a channel open even as it has downplayed safety
insights.locator: Can the United States and China

insights.claim: Daniel Remler argues that the belief that US-China cooperation on AI safety can be siloed off entirely from competition is fanciful, because any AI risk dialogue takes place within the broader strategic competition.
insights.speaker: Daniel Remler
insights.so_what: Do not price in a stable AI-safety détente; AI policy outcomes will track the broader rivalry (export controls, chips).
insights.quote: a belief as appealing as it is fanciful
insights.locator: Can the United States and China

insights.claim: Remler's headline thesis is that China's AI diplomacy is working and that the United States should learn from it.
insights.speaker: Daniel Remler
insights.so_what: Chinese AI influence with third countries may be gaining ground — watch adoption of Chinese models/standards abroad.
